facts.text: The 'Werewolf Break' borrows from showman William Castle, who pioneered the 'Fright Break' pause in Homicidal (1961). Reviewer Richard Scheib of Moria points to the Castle link.
The Land Rover in the opening is a 1973 Series III 109. Cheap Amicus movies still got fancy wheels: a mint one can fetch $40,000 or more today.
Cameras rolled on The Beast Must Die on July 16, 1973 at Shepperton Studios outside London. Trade charts suggest the shoot wrapped by early September, a quick Amicus-style schedule.
Calvin Lockhart's hunting rifle is a Griffin & Howe M1903 Sporter, a custom handmade gun that today costs $13,500 and up.
Vampire star Robert Quarry (Count Yorga) was first slated for the lead. Producers switched to Calvin Lockhart at the last minute to cash in on the blaxploitation craze.
Anton Diffring (Pavel) admitted he'd never watched Doctor Who. He took his 1988 guest role mainly to be in London for Wimbledon.
Producers considered Herbert Lom, Patrick Magee, Donald Pleasence and Charles Gray, among others, for Pavel before Anton Diffring got the job.
Charles Gray (Bennington) played a Bond ally in You Only Live Twice, then Bond's arch-villain Blofeld in Diamonds Are Forever. He's also the Criminologist in The Rocky Horror Picture Show.
According to director Paul Annett, the part of Caroline was meant for singer Dame Shirley Bassey. She was unavailable, so Marlene Clark was hired on Calvin Lockhart's suggestion.
Marlene Clark's voice was dubbed by Annie Ross, the jazz singer of Lambert, Hendricks & Ross.
Calvin Lockhart was the first black actor to play leads with the Royal Shakespeare Company. He'd studied to be a civil engineer at Cooper Union first.
Peter Cushing's boots for Star Wars (1977) hurt, so he wore slippers and George Lucas shot him from the waist up. Here he plays lycanthropy expert Dr. Lundgren.
Dr. Lundgren (Peter Cushing) blames werewolfism on the lymphatic glands. In James Blish's original story, its psychiatrist Lundgren blames a mutation of the pineal gland in the brain instead.
The film is based on James Blish's 1950 story 'There Shall Be No Darkness'. Blish himself called it 'a schoolboy pastiche of Dracula.'
Richard Scheib of Moria says the whodunnit angle is weak. He writes the werewolf 'could have been chosen by randomly drawing straws.'
Dr. Lundgren, played by Peter Cushing, says wolfsbane doesn't grow in Britain. It's actually native there and has been recorded since the first century AD.
Caroline is played by Marlene Clark, star of the cult vampire film Ganja & Hess (1973). She later played Lamont's girlfriend Janet on the sitcom Sanford and Son.
Hammer and Amicus each made only one werewolf film in 20 years of horror. Hammer's was The Curse of the Werewolf (1961), starring Oliver Reed. Amicus's was this one.
Casting dark-skinned Calvin Lockhart caused real trouble: the many day-for-night scenes, shot in daylight with filters, were hard to light. Director Paul Annett discusses this on his commentary.
Around 1972, Robert Shaw wanted the lead. He was in a career lull with big bills to pay, and Don Sharp was then the intended director.
British Horror Films notes that millionaire Tom Newcliffe's skin colour is never remarked on in the story, which was unusual for a 1974 film with a Black lead like Calvin Lockhart.
Moria's Richard Scheib notes werewolf whodunnits are rare. He cites Universal's The Undying Monster (1942) as the first, and guesses Amicus was inspired by Murder on the Orient Express (1974).
Peter Cushing was nicknamed 'Props' for using small objects to make his acting natural. He'd often hand directors a list of what his character carried in his pockets.
Goof spotted by IMDb users: with the alarm going off, Tom could simply check his spy cameras to see which guest is missing from their room. The thought never seems to occur to him.
This was the only theatrical feature directed by Paul Annett, who mostly worked in TV. He later directed episodes of Secret Army and Tales of the Unexpected.
Pavel (Anton Diffring) grabs a stainless steel Walther PPK, James Bond's gun. The helicopter pilot later carries one too.
On a small budget the werewolf is a German Shepherd in a fur costume. The Pop-up team's view: it's the first film where a dog fights a werewolf, and the dog survived long after filming.
Mondo Digital says the Werewolf Break gimmick echoes the 1960s Ten Little Indians adaptation, which also stopped to let viewers guess whodunit. Film is a mashup of that and The Most Dangerous Game.
The red car Tom disables is a 1966 Ford Galaxie 500, a rare Canadian-built model made for the UK market.
Before Charles Gray got the role of Bennington, producers considered Patrick Troughton, Michael Gough, Richard Todd, Joss Ackland and Jeremy Kemp, among others.
The helicopter, an Alouette II (G-AWFY), also appears in Conflict (1973). It was sold to Italy and crashed into a cable in 1984, killing all four aboard.
Calvin Lockhart's submachine gun is a Swiss Rexim-Favor Mk5, of which only about 2,000 were made. Similar props were later used in Star Wars (1977) and Alien (1979).
Per Mondo Digital's review of the Blu-ray, producer Max J. Rosenberg said the script shifted from a dark fantasy into a whodunit. Rosenberg and Milton Subotsky were both lukewarm on the result.
Britain's Monthly Film Bulletin found the Werewolf Break 'amusing enough', bringing 'old-time fairground entertainment', but said Amicus still needed a good scriptwriter.
The Hollywood Reporter's Alan R. Howard reviewed the film on its April 24, 1974 Los Angeles opening. He thought the movie could stand on its own merits without the audience-guessing gimmick.
facts.byline: Alan R. Howard — The Hollywood Reporter

facts.text: The music during the Werewolf Break is 'Think!', composed by Merv Griffin for the game show Jeopardy!
Director Paul Annett hated the Werewolf Break: 'It stopped the film stone dead.' Producer Milton Subotsky added it over his objections.
The film also circulated on home video as 'Black Werewolf', a cut without the Werewolf Break.
The 2021 horror comedy Werewolves Within spoofs this film, a whodunnit among suspects trapped together.
Goof: Tom says he has one silver bullet left. But earlier he handed each guest a silver bullet for a test and never collected them, so he could have gone out with most of a full clip.
This was the last Amicus horror film made with co-founder Milton Subotsky, and one of the few not built as an anthology.
The UK's BBFC gave it an X certificate. In the US, Cinerama Releasing opened it in April 1974 with a mild PG rating, despite the throat-ripping.
The Break is narrated by actor Valentine Dyall, per We Belong Dead. Ciaran Madden (Davina) later played Michael Gambon's wife in the TV series Maigret.
